note: Matching a pitch from a hum: the low Do and then Sol over a drone, each hummed with lips closed and opened to "oo" on the same note. The why says why a hum is easy to tune, the drill stays at 3 minutes with one care line, and the key is moves, with a {{?key}} line on what stays the same.

exercise.title: Hum, then open to "oo"
exercise.why: Humming keeps the sound small and easy to tune, so opening to "oo" from a hum carries the in-tune note with it.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff. Hum the low {{1}} with your lips closed, then open the hum to "oo" on the same note.
Then skip up to {{5}} the same way: hum it first, then open it to "oo".
Practice until your line stays flat on the staff as the hum opens.
_Don't reach for high notes: the {{5}} here is the one just above the low {{1}}._
{{?key}}In another key the drone sits higher or lower, and the hum still opens on the same note.
